note: Embed the query, cosine nearest-neighbours over pgvector. Strong on paraphrase and cross-lingual; blind to exact tokens like the cultivar code WL-323. The number every later stage has to beat.

Exact-term match via tsvector + ts_rank_cd. Scored 0.00 until the AND->OR tsquery fix (websearch_to_tsquery ANDs every term, so a whole-question query matched nothing). Honest result: its answer@5 edge over hybrid (0.50 vs 0.45) is a single question -- within noise at n=20 -- but doc@5 shows a real four-document gap (0.85 vs 0.65): equal-weight RRF was diluting the stronger lexical retriever's recall into the pool. That gap, not the noisy answer@5, is why the project did not stop at hybrid.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (1/(k+60)): fuses the two rankings by position, sidestepping the incomparable cosine-vs-ts_rank score scales. Fixed q05 and q14 over the dense baseline. Gets meaning AND exact codes -- but answer@1 DROPS to 0.15 (below dense's 0.30) and mrr@5 to 0.25: equal-weight RRF pushes the true answer out of the #1 slot, buying pool recall at the cost of top-1 precision. That is exactly what the reranker exists to fix.

Re-scores the top-20 (query, chunk) candidates read together, keeps the top 5. Fixed 6 questions hybrid missed (q01, q02, q03, q09, q16, q21) with ZERO regressions -- the decisive precision win. The ordering gain answer@5 hides: answer@1 jumps 0.15->0.75 and mrr@5 0.25->0.75 -- whenever the answer is in the pool the reranker pins it to rank 1 (here answer@1 == answer@5). Still misses q07, q08, q15, q20, q22. A candidate-pool sweep (eval/sweep_candidates.py) pinpoints why: q07/q15/q20/q22 are not in hybrid's top-60 at all -- true recall gaps for the embedder lever, not pool size -- while only q08 sits deeper (hybrid rank 46), recoverable solely by tripling the candidate pool (+1 question at ~3x rerank latency, so candidates stays at 20). Measured by eval/compare_retrievers.py over the answerable golden set.
